# Cones generated by rotation and dilation characteristics

↑ **Parent:** [Method of characteristics](method-of-characteristics.md)

For a fixed real unit [vector](vector.md) $k$, the linear [ordinary differential equation](ordinary-differential-equation.md) $\dot r=r-k\times r$ combines [dilation](uniform-dilation.md) with [rotation](rotation-mathematics.md) about the axis $\mathbb Rk$. Its solution from a line $s\ell$, with $|\ell|=1$, is

$$
r(s,t)=se^t\bigl(\kappa k+\cos t\,v-\sin t\,(k\times v)\bigr),\qquad\kappa=k\cdot\ell,\quad v=\ell-\kappa k.
$$

Since $k\cdot r=se^t\kappa$ and $|r|=|s|e^t$, the union of these [characteristic curves](characteristic-curve.md) is given by $|k\cdot r|=|\kappa||r|$. For $0<|\kappa|<1$ it is a circular [cone](cone-geometry.md) of semi-angle $\arccos|\kappa|$: varying $t$ supplies every azimuth and varying $s$ supplies every radius on both halves. For $\kappa=0$ it is a [plane](plane.md); for $|\kappa|=1$ it is only the axis. In the last case the line is itself a [characteristic curve](characteristic-curve.md), so the [initial data](initial-condition.md) do not generate a two-dimensional [surface](topological-surface-split.md). The cone is a [smooth surface](smooth-surface.md) away from its vertex, and it is a [graph of a function](graph-of-a-function.md) only on suitable patches. Invariance of a graph patch under [characteristic curves](characteristic-curve.md) holds only while the curve stays in its domain; global flow invariance requires continuation of that patch.
